title: India's Defence Production Hits Record ₹1.78 Lakh Crore as Private Sector Share Reaches All-Time High
excerpt: Annual defence output surged 15.6% in FY 2025-26, with indigenous production nearly four-fold since 2013-14 and exports reaching a record ₹38,424 crore.
body:
• India's annual defence production reached an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, up 15.6% from the previous year and 110% since FY 2020-21.
  • Indigenous defence production has grown nearly four-fold from ₹43,746 crore in FY 2013-14, reflecting the Aatmanirbhar Bharat push.
  • The private sector's share hit a record 24%, with contributions reaching approximately ₹42,000 crore — up from 22% the previous year.
  • Defence exports surged to a record ₹38,424 crore, and the government targets ₹3 lakh crore in total production and ₹50,000 crore in exports within the next two to three years.

India's defence manufacturing sector posted its strongest year on record in FY 2025-26, with annual production surging to ₹1.78 lakh crore — a 15.6% jump over the previous fiscal year and a milestone that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh credited to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and the broader Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

The Numbers

The latest figure, announced by the Ministry of Defence in June, marks a 110% increase from FY 2020-21, when defence production stood at ₹84,643 crore. More strikingly, indigenous production has grown nearly four-fold from ₹43,746 crore recorded in FY 2013-14, the year before the current government took office.

Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and other public sector units accounted for approximately 76% of total output. The private sector contributed the remaining 24%, its highest share ever, with production reaching roughly ₹42,000 crore — up from 22% in FY 2024-25.

"This represents not just a rise in numbers, but a growth in India's capabilities. It signifies a boost in the nation's self-confidence."

— Rajnath Singh, Defence Minister of India

Exports Hit Record

The production surge has fed directly into India's growing defence export business. Defence exports reached a record ₹38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, underscoring India's transition from a predominantly import-dependent defence market to an increasingly competitive exporter. India now exports military hardware and components to dozens of countries, a sharp departure from a decade ago when the country was the world's largest arms importer.

Corporatization Pays Off

Speaking at an event at Ordnance Factory Ambajhari in Nagpur, Singh highlighted the impact of the 2021 corporatization of the Ordnance Factory Board (OFB). Production across the seven new Defence Public Sector Units created from the OFB rose from ₹12,755 crore in the pre-corporatization year of FY 2019-20 to ₹26,282 crore in FY 2025-26. Defence exports from these units surged from ₹81 crore to ₹4,561 crore in the same period.

Singh emphasized that self-reliance in defence manufacturing was not merely an economic goal but a strategic imperative. "A nation capable of meeting its own requirements moves forward with the greatest confidence towards safeguarding its interests," he said, adding that emerging technologies had altered the very definition of warfare.

Ambitious Targets Ahead

The government has set targets of ₹3 lakh crore in annual defence production and ₹50,000 crore in defence exports within the next two to three years. Singh said the targets could be achieved ahead of schedule, citing sustained policy support, new initiatives, increased private sector participation, and growing export capabilities.

The push has been backed by a series of policy measures, including positive indigenization lists that ban the import of hundreds of defence items, dedicated defence industrial corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and streamlined licensing for private manufacturers. The government has also increased the foreign direct investment limit in defence to 74% through the automatic route.

What It Means

The growth trajectory positions India as an emerging player in the global defence supply chain, though it still lags behind the United States, China, Russia, and major European producers in absolute terms. For India's defence industrial base — which includes both legacy public sector giants like Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Bharat Electronics, and a growing cohort of private firms — the numbers signal a structural shift that has been years in the making.
